answer.says: Shri Hegde, I have no food in the house, and Ramesh has not been paid to cook. I have only ninety-six rupees on me. If you will allow me to eat what is left of your dinner, I will pay you ten rupees. Ramesh, you may wait; I have nothing to give you tonight.
answer.thought: The hunger is a physical fact that negates my abstract dignity. I am reduced to begging a fellow German for scraps while the man who serves me waits in silence, unpaid. The ethical idea is not actual here; it is a hunger I cannot satisfy with my own pocket. I must eat to continue, even if it means eating from another's plate.
